newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-C-C Amatil signs San Miguel deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-C-C Amatil signs San Miguel deal.

text.p: Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd (CCA) said on Wednesday it had signed definitive agreements with San Miguel Corp of the Philippines and The Coca-Cola Co for the exchange of CCA shares for all of the common shares of Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc.

The deal had created some concern among San Miguel shareholders about Philippines representation on the board of C-C Amatil and this had prompted some fears that the completion of the A$3.4 billion transaction could be delayed.

C-C Amatil said San Miguel would be invited to accept four positions on the C-C Amatil board after the issue of the 293 million shares in question. Following completion of the deal, subject to an extraordinary general meeting, San Miguel will hold 25 percent of C-C Amatil and The Coca-Cola Co 33 percent.

C-C Amatil said that if C-C Bottlers Philippines had been included in its 1996 results, sales volume would have been 1.1 billion unit cases and net profit would have doubled to A$286 million. Independent expert Grant Samuel and Associates concluded the transaction was fair and reasonable to those shareholders not associated with the parties to the deal.
Completion of the transaction is also conditional upon all relevant government and regulatory approvals having been obtained in Australia, the Philippines and the USA.
Approval by the Australian Foreign Investment Review Board has already been received.
By 10.55 p.m. (0055 GMT), C-C Amatil shares were 62 cents higher at A$16.02, their highest level since November 1996 when it issued a profit warning on its 1996 year result.
